drug_class: HPPD enzyme inhibitor (a medicine that blocks a specific enzyme in the body)
purpose: Nitisinone is used to treat a rare inherited condition called Hereditary Tyrosinemia Type 1 (HT-1), where the body cannot properly break down an amino acid called tyrosine. Without treatment, harmful substances build up and can seriously damage the liver and kidneys. This medicine helps prevent that damage and is usually used along with a special low-tyrosine, low-phenylalanine diet.
how_it_works: Your body breaks down tyrosine through a series of steps, and in HT-1, one of those steps is broken, causing toxic substances to build up. Nitisinone works by blocking an earlier step in this process, which stops those harmful toxic substances from forming in the first place. Think of it like shutting off a faucet upstream to prevent a toxic flood downstream.
common_side_effects: Eye problems such as eye pain, redness, or sensitivity to light are the most important side effects to watch for. You may also notice low platelet or white blood cell counts (found on blood tests), which your doctor will monitor regularly. Other side effects can include itching or skin rash.
warnings: While taking this medicine, you MUST follow a strict low-tyrosine and low-phenylalanine diet — otherwise tyrosine levels in your blood can get too high and cause serious eye damage, including corneal ulcers. Tell your doctor right away if you notice any changes in your vision or eye discomfort. Regular blood tests and eye exams are very important while on this medicine. Keep all follow-up appointments with your care team.
typical_dosing: The dose is based on your body weight and is usually taken once or twice a day by mouth as a capsule or tablet. Capsules can be opened and mixed with a small amount of food like applesauce if swallowing is difficult. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on blood tests and how well the medicine is working for you.
